req.title: Rate limit not enforced
req.statement: The system shall not throttle single-client request rates below 60/min.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-039 states the system shall NOT throttle single-client request rates below 60/min, meaning all 60 requests within a minute window must succeed with HTTP 2xx. Tests cover: (1) positive — 60 rapid sequential requests all return 2xx (EP: normal burst within allowed rate); (2) negative — a single malformed request returns 4xx, confirming error-path handling is distinct from rate-limiting (NEG); (3) boundary — exactly 60 requests succeed and none are rejected with 429 (BVA at the threshold). Each test uses FastAPI TestClient in-process, issues real HTTP calls, and asserts exact status codes to catch mutations on comparison operators and constants.

tests.name: test_60_requests_all_succeed_positive
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
No rate-limiting middleware is active that would block < 60 req/min
actions: Send 60 consecutive GET /tasks/ requests using TestClient
expected: No response has status code 429 or any 4xx/5xx
trace: R-TASK-039: system shall not throttle single-client request rates below 60/min
EP: 60 requests is within the allowed partition; all must succeed
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_60_requests_all_succeed_positive():
    client = TestClient(app)
    responses = [client.get("/tasks/") for _ in range(60)]
    status_codes = [r.status_code for r in responses]
    assert len(status_codes) == 60
    for i, code in enumerate(status_codes):
        assert code == 200, f"Request {i+1} returned {code}, expected 200"
    assert all(c == 200 for c in status_codes)
    assert 429 not in status_codes

test_60_requests_all_succeed_positive()

tests.name: test_malformed_request_returns_4xx_not_rate_limited
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
actions: Send a POST /tasks/ request with an empty body (missing required 'title' field)
Inspect the response status code and body
expected: Response status code is 422 (Unprocessable Entity) — a client error, not a rate-limit error
trace: R-TASK-039: error pathway is HTTP 4xx on client error
NEG: a bad request must return 4xx for client-error reasons, not be confused with rate-limiting
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_malformed_request_returns_4xx_not_rate_limited():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r = client.post("/tasks/", json={})
    assert r.status_code == 422
    assert r.status_code != 429
    assert r.status_code != 200
    assert r.status_code != 201
    body = r.json()
    assert "detail" in body

test_malformed_request_returns_4xx_not_rate_limited()

tests.name: test_exactly_60_requests_boundary_all_2xx
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
The rate limit threshold per requirement is 60 requests per minute
actions: Send exactly 59 GET /tasks/ requests and verify all succeed
Send the 60th GET /tasks/ request and verify it also succeeds
Confirm no request in the set of 60 was rejected
expected: No response in the 60-request batch returns 429 or any non-2xx code
trace: R-TASK-039: system shall not throttle below 60/min — boundary is exactly 60
BVA: test at threshold-1 (59), threshold (60); both must succeed; catches off-by-one mutations on the constant 60
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_exactly_60_requests_boundary_all_2xx():
    client = TestClient(app)
    THRESHOLD = 60
    responses_59 = [client.get("/tasks/") for _ in range(THRESHOLD - 1)]
    for i, r in enumerate(responses_59):
        assert r.status_code == 200, f"Request {i+1} of 59 returned {r.status_code}"
    r60 = client.get("/tasks/")
    assert r60.status_code == 200, f"60th request returned {r60.status_code}, expected 200"
    all_responses = responses_59 + [r60]
    assert len(all_responses) == 60
    non_2xx = [r.status_code for r in all_responses if not (200 <= r.status_code < 300)]
    assert non_2xx == [], f"Non-2xx responses found: {non_2xx}"
    assert 429 not in [r.status_code for r in all_responses]

test_exactly_60_requests_boundary_all_2xx()

tests.name: test_mixed_endpoints_60_requests_all_succeed
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
Pre-loaded tasks with ids 1-20 exist in the database
Rate limit applies per client across endpoint types
actions: Send 60 requests alternating between GET /tasks/ and GET /tasks/1
trace: R-TASK-039: rate limit not enforced — any single-client request pattern up to 60/min must succeed
EP: mixed-endpoint burst is within the allowed equivalence class
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_mixed_endpoints_60_requests_all_succeed():
    client = TestClient(app)
    responses = []
    for i in range(60):
        if i % 2 == 0:
            r = client.get("/tasks/")
        else:
            r = client.get("/tasks/1")
        responses.append(r)
    assert len(responses) == 60
    status_codes = [r.status_code for r in responses]
    assert 429 not in status_codes
    for i, code in enumerate(status_codes):
        assert code == 200, f"Request {i+1} returned {code}"

test_mixed_endpoints_60_requests_all_succeed()

tests.name: test_post_requests_within_rate_limit_all_succeed
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
Rate limit applies to write operations as well as reads
actions: Send 20 valid POST /tasks/ requests in rapid succession
expected: All 20 POST responses return status code 201
Each response body contains the created task with a valid id
trace: R-TASK-039: rate limit not enforced for any request type below 60/min
DT: decision table covers write-path requests; 20 POSTs is well within 60/min threshold
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

def test_post_requests_within_rate_limit_all_succeed():
    client = TestClient(app)
    responses = []
    for i in range(20):
        payload = {"title": f"Rate test task {i}", "completed": False}
        r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
        responses.append(r)
    assert len(responses) == 20
    status_codes = [r.status_code for r in responses]
    assert 429 not in status_codes
    for i, r in enumerate(responses):
        assert r.status_code == 201, f"POST {i+1} returned {r.status_code}"
        body = r.json()
        assert "id" in body
        assert body["id"] >= 21

test_post_requests_within_rate_limit_all_succeed()
